How to Join a WhatsApp group on Android?

  1. To join a WhatsApp group on Android: Search for the group link, select your preferred group, and open its link.
  2. Check group details by reading the description, looking at the profile picture, and reviewing the rules and member count. If the group seems genuine, continue. If you notice spam or irrelevant content, do not join.
  3. Tap ‘Join’. After you tap, you will become a member of the group and be able to participate in discussions.
  4. Introduce yourself in the group and state your purpose for joining. Read existing messages, view photos and videos, and participate as you wish.
  5. Stay safe: Avoid clicking suspicious links. Confirm group security with the admin. If you find an invalid link, request a new one from the website owner.

How to leave a WhatsApp Group:

  1. Select the group: First, select the group you want to leave. You can search for it in WhatsApp’s search bar for instant access. After that, open the group chat by clicking on the group name or icon.
  2. Tap the Group Name: Click the group name. You will see three different options.
  3. Scroll down:  Scroll the page down. You will see the “Exit group” button.
  4. Tap “Exit Button”: click the exit button to remove yourself from the group. After you hit the button, you will see “You are no longer a member of this group”. It means you have successfully left the group.
  5. Delete the Group: Tap the group, then press it for a second. You see the bar button above: Delete. Click on it to remove the group from the list.

Privacy features of WhatsApp groups

  1. End-to-End Encryption for Group Chats: WhatsApp’s end-to-end encryption prevents anyone outside the group from seeing photos, videos, text, or files. That is why millions of communities worldwide prefer WhatsApp groups for online collaboration.

  3. Ability to Mute Group Notifications: Users can mute notifications from WhatsApp groups to maintain their personal digital space. This feature helps user to focus on their daily routine work without any interpretation.
  4. Group Admin Approval for New Members: The group admin always controls the whole group. On WhatsApp, only the group admin can add or remove members. Other members cannot interpret in this setting, helping the group to avoid irrelevant members. It helps build trust among members and within the group, making the WhatsApp group more valuable.
  5. Chat Lock Feature for Sensitive Conversations: In a new update, WhatsApp now offers users secure, encrypted group conversations with password, fingerprint, or device authentication. This privacy layer helps members participate in group discussions without hesitation about privacy.
  6. Disappearing Messages for Temporary Discussions: WhatsApp can automatically delete conversations within 24 hours using the Disappearing Messages feature. This helps users delete sensitive conversations and temporary content from the device without having to go into the settings every time.
  7. Blocking and Reporting Suspicious Users: If anyone sends you a suspicious message, text, or call, you can report and block that user within minutes. Just click the report button on his profile and block him to stop his spam activity. You can also block unknown numbers and harmful accounts. They cannot send messages or make calls now, and also can’t view your profile pictures.
  8. Secure Backup: WhatsApp offers a secure, end-to-end-encrypted backup feature that lets users protect their chat history and group conversations.
